gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-kr: Edo SZ draws its lowercase like bent spaghetti, one constant line with real iron stature. Noto Sans KR sits beneath it with generous curve openings and stubby ascenders, and a slightly smaller size lets that big x-height settle.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lao: Classic and cultural, Edo SZ runs a single unbroken line weight from terminals to junctions, like wire. And Noto Sans Lao follows with a tall x-height and open mouths, giving that wiry heading a modern, easygoing partner underneath.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lao-loope: Noto Sans Lao Looped sets words as solid blocks, with bowls left unfinished on one side, under Edo SZ's hairline-free lettering. Text comes across dense, modern and smooth.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable is how Noto Sans Lepcha feels, with wide curve openings throughout. Edo SZ is best at looking like letters bent from a single wire, while the body font is best at staying open and easy for sustained text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu reads with tall-bodied small letters and curves that gape wide open, friendly and contemporary. But Edo SZ keeps a steady pen pressure from first letter to last, so the heading stays a single confident line above it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu reads tidy and plain, with tiny gaps between ascender tops and the x-height line. Noto Sans Lisu also opens its s curves wide, so a long stretch of text moves along smoothly beneath Edo SZ's spaghetti-like lettering.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Tails and terminals as thick as the stems give Edo SZ its tube-like, cultural look. And Noto Sans Lydian runs below with capitals barely taller than lowercase and a wide, springy opening, so extended text feels friendly and level.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Edo SZ looks like thin steel rod bent into every letter, with classic cast-iron stature in the lowercase. Noto Sans Mahajani follows with tall lowercase and a funnel-wide e, so longer text moves easily.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Looped wire above, roomy text below. Edo SZ bends strokes like thin plastic tubing, and Noto Sans Malayalam answers with a dominant middle zone and an openly bending s, so the two feel clearly different yet friendly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Edo SZ draws every stroke at one thickness, giving its lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Mandaic loosens things with lowercase rising close to capitals and unclamped curves.
